My goal is to maximize my value. I know my final match will be my favorite school from my "obtainable set". The obtainable set is determined by my priority rank at each school.

At school w, my priority is 1. This is the highest priority, so w is very likely in my obtainable set.
At school x, my priority is 2. This is a lower priority, so x might not be in my obtainable set.
At school y, my priority is 1. This is the highest priority, so y is very likely in my obtainable set.
At school z, my priority is 2. This is a lower priority, so z might not be in my obtainable set.

My values are w = $69, x = $52, y = $56, z = $64.

I want to rank the schools in decreasing order of value, but with consideration for their likelihood of being obtainable. Since w and y are very likely obtainable, I should rank the higher value of these two first. w has a higher value than y, so I should rank w first.

Next, I need to consider whether to rank y or z next. z has a higher value than y, however, y has a higher priority than z. Since I want to maximize my value, but only from the obtainable set, I should rank y second.

Finally, I need to rank z and x. z has a higher value than x. Therefore, I should rank z before x.

Thus, my ranking should be w > y > z > x.

The most important thing is to consider the possibility of being rejected by both w and y. In that case, I want to be matched to z rather than x.

Therefore, I should rank the schools in the order of my preferences, but prioritizing the schools where I have a higher priority.

I should rank w first, because it is my most preferred school. If I get in, great.
Then I should rank y, my second most preferred school. If I get in, great.
Then I should rank z, since I have priority 1 there and prefer it to x.
Finally, I rank x last.
